subtasks: S1 outcome-label seam: DELIVERED (feat/p3-s1-outcome-label-seam, 5e7b43b5). The five metric keys stop being a literal in the caller and become one exported contract (WEAK_LABEL_METRIC_KEYS + build_weak_label) that analyst calls; the always-empty back-fill now says so in prose instead of reading like working code. The gap itself is registered as a test that goes red when metrics start arriving, and every scanner in that test has a positive control because a claim whose value is zero cannot have one built in. 8 cases, mutation self-check 11/11.

S2 link result from projection to fact: DELIVERED (feat/p3-s2-link-from-projection-to-fact, c27b2f1e). The request-scoped matching in analytics.py is now one pure function, and the link is finally written down. backend/services/publish_identity.py owns the whole rule: normalize_platform_post_id (moved verbatim out of analytics -- same semantics, one owner instead of a copy on each side) plus resolve_platform_links, which returns a frozen LinkResolution of index pairs so a caller applies the decision to its own rows. That is what makes the link recomputable: no I/O, no mutation, so the same inputs give the same answer inside a request or in a sync job. evaluator_samples gained a nullable platform_post_id on both schema paths (CREATE TABLE plus the idempotent ALTER), and record_publish_identity is the single writer, called from the publisher node's one exit -- the only place holding both the thread and the published id, with evaluator_gate -> publish_gate -> publisher guaranteeing the sample exists first. 26 cases in tests/unit/services/test_publish_identity.py. TWO TICKET PREMISES WERE REFUTED BY RECONNAISSANCE (prd.md section 11): adding the column is NOT necessary to join the two sides -- backfill_engagement keys on thread_id alone, and analyst's thread_id, publisher's workflow_thread_id and analytics' _extract_post_data all resolve to the same value -- so the column's real value is making S3's REVERSE lookup (note_id -> sample) an index hit; and the free path already persists weak labels (free.py's get_analytics back-fills evaluator_samples.engagement with no link_status gate), so the gap was never 'nothing persists', it was 'the workflow path has no deterministic source of real metrics'. ONE BUG THE REFACTOR INTRODUCED AND THE TESTS CAUGHT: LinkGroup.status's first draft returned unmatched for 'no workflow claim + several imported claims on that id', where the old code reached its ambiguous branch; it is now explicit and carries both a table row and a mutant (M03). Not fixed: publisher's write-side startswith('mock_') guard (changing the stored value would move the publish contract, and the read side normalizes before comparing), and get_analytics' ungated back-fill (a write-frequency question for S3/S4). GATES: ruff 542 / format 542 / mypy 217 / baseline drift / tool gate all green; full pytest 3612 passed, 3 skipped (+26). MUTATION SELF-CHECK 14/14 killed, step 0 OK, restore=OK.

S3 close the edge: DELIVERED (feat/p3-s3-sync-weak-label-backfill, 24453cf9). The gap was never chicken-and-egg -- it was a missing producer. The only writer of evaluator_samples.engagement (backfill_engagement) was reached from analyst, which reads metrics out of a publish-time publish_result, a payload carrying identity and status only; so engagement stayed NULL, count_labeled_since stayed 0 and maybe_evolve never left below threshold on a system that was fully wired and fully green. The creator-stats import knows both the post id and its real counts, so the seam is closed from that end. evaluator_config gains a shared clause (_ATTACH_WEAK_LABEL_SQL) plus ENGAGEMENT_LABEL_SOURCE, so the two writers differ only in WHICH ROWS they pick, never in WHAT they write; backfill_engagement_for_posts selects by platform_post_id, runs one transaction and returns the summed rowcount -- deliberately not the number of posts, since most imported notes were never judged. backfill_engagement also rewrites provenance, which is a correction rather than new semantics: label_source='evaluator' was already false in the database, because insert_sample writes it at judgement time and engagement arrives in a later UPDATE. pipeline wires the attach at import_bundle's single exit, after persist; the post id is normalized producer-side (normalize_platform_post_id stays the one owner) and the payload goes through build_weak_label (one declaration, shared with analyst). 27 cases. MUTATION SELF-CHECK FOUND AND FIXED A REAL HOLE: the end-to-end fixture read the expected label from the import instead of parsing it out of the statement it was executing, so dropping the label from the shared clause -- or writing the wrong value -- left the whole 'real write -> real counter -> evolved' chain green; M1 was only 3 red, all of them db-layer or keyword assertions. After the fixture parses the label out of the SQL: M1 -> 8 red (5 from the end-to-end file), M2 -> 4 red. That failure shape is worth naming: a fixture answering FOR the statement under test is a third variant of 'structurally complete, never started' (the first two being a column with no writer and a branch with no producer). TWO TICKET PREMISES REFUTED (prd.md section 13): the sync side has no consumer of the link result, so this slice builds a producer rather than using one; and label_source had ZERO readers before this slice (fetch_labeled_samples and count_labeled_since both filter on engagement IS NOT NULL and never look at it), so the only observable change here is the count and the evolution -- label_source=engagement is a key the ticket imagined for downstream, not something this slice makes any behaviour depend on. Check 4 of the S1 contract test did NOT go red, and that is correct: the sync path never builds a publish result. REGISTERED, NOT FIXED: the refit window is the sample's creation time, so a backfill can label an old row successfully and move the counter by zero (case 8); the free path's ungated backfill is a write-condition question (section 11); and the ordering comment on _attach_real_weak_labels is an intent claim, not a guaranteed property -- the tests cannot tell the two orders apart.

S4 contract and the gate condition: DELIVERED (feat/p3-s4-outcome-learning-contract, d0f33c08). docs/outcome-learning.md is the contract document and it is pinned by recomputation rather than by anchors. The repository already had two shapes for turning a document into a gate, and the shape follows the content: docs/execution-plane.md publishes LOCATIONS, so test_docs_anchors.py pins it with file:line anchors plus a row-count floor, because a line is only ever checked and never enumerated, so deleting one leaves no trace; docs/planning.md publishes FACTS, so test_planning_claims.py pins it with claim-table marker blocks holding an id -> callable table that recomputes each value from the code. Pinning a fact by location fails in the wrong direction -- the net goes red when a line moves and stays green when a number changes. S4 publishes facts (a key set, how many writers share one clause, the refit threshold, which column the window filters on), so it took the second shape, and the document publishes no file:line at all: a renamed symbol is visible (the import breaks, ruff and mypy complain) while a changed number is silent. NO ROW-COUNT FLOOR IS NEEDED HERE, and that follows from the third closed-loop check rather than from an oversight: the recalculators are themselves the enumeration, so a dropped row surfaces as an orphaned checker and the test fires. THE FIRST THING THE CHECKERS CAUGHT WAS MY OWN TABLE LYING. Two claims assert that something is absent, and I had published one as true (semantic polarity) and the other as false (raw-substring polarity), so the table contradicted the prose immediately beside it, which says the selector does NOT skip already-labelled rows. A recalculator can be negated in place, but then not scanner(...) and scanner(...) read identically in the claim table; the fix was to NAME the direction (_sql_omits) so the id, the published value and the scan all point the same way. That was the first red run: count_ignores_when_the_label_arrived publishes true but recomputes to false. THE ONE RULING (document section 4). The write condition is once per sync while the refit window is the sample's creation time, so a sample judged before the active epoch can be labelled successfully and still move the counter by zero. Three candidates were weighed: switch the window to when the label arrived, narrow the write condition to samples created after the epoch, or keep it and register the evidence requirement. The third was taken, because the first is the DANGEROUS direction rather than the safe one: creator_note_stats is an upsert, so a note re-syncs and re-back-fills repeatedly, and under an arrival-time window every repeat write would count as a new label -- inflating the count and risking a refit on an immature sample pool. Late merely delays; wrong contaminates the weights. The evidence requirement is recorded instead: to reopen this, first show that a repeated back-fill of the same row is distinguishable from a new label (a back-fill counter or a label version), which does not exist today. The mismatch is itself pinned by count_ignores_when_the_label_arrived, so it goes red if anyone quietly changes the filter. ALSO DELIVERED: the four comments above WEAK_LABEL_METRIC_KEYS that S3 turned into lies are corrected -- they still said the analyst node was the only writer, that nothing produces the keys today, that label_source=engagement had no writer, and that wiring them through was a later slice's job. ZERO OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: one comment block, one document, one test file; no production path, contract or schema touched. That is the correct shape for a contract slice. 8 CASES: four closed-loop (each published claim recomputes, each claim has a recalculator, each recalculator is published, the markers are balanced) and four positive controls, because a claim asserting an absence cannot carry a control inside it -- a scanner gutted to return False stays green -- so every absence scanner takes a root argument and is pointed at a fixture where the thing IS present. TWO SCANNING TRAPS, both found by measurement and both written into the docstring: label_source has two spellings (a keyword argument on the insert path, which has TWO writers, versus a value inside shared SQL on the attach path), so no single scan covers both; and maybe_evolve uses BOTH shapes for its action value (a dict literal and a subscript assignment), so scanning one shape reports a subset that looks complete -- scanning subscripts alone yields error and evolved while silently dropping skip. THE BLOCK COUNT IS 3, NOT 4, AND THAT WAS MY CONSTANT BEING STOPPED BY THE HARNESS: the mutation script asserted hits=4 on the markers and the run aborted with outcome-learning.md anchor occurs 3x wanted 4 -- worth recording as evidence that an anchor assertion is more reliable than recollection. (8 + 7 + 5 = 20 claims.) GATES: ruff 544 / format 544 / mypy 217 / baseline drift within threshold / tool gate OK; full pytest 3631 passed, 3 skipped (+8). MUTATION SELF-CHECK 17/17 KILLED, baseline green, restore byte-identical: 7 document-side (a number edited, a set member dropped, a row added with no checker, a row deleted leaving an orphan, one id published twice, one end marker renamed so the pairs go unbalanced, and both markers of one block renamed so the pairs stay balanced while the rows vanish -- the last two are a pair, one testing balance and the other testing that balance is not safety), 8 code-side (the threshold moved, the import asking for a refit unconditionally, the selector starting to skip labelled rows, the count window dropping its created_at filter, the count gaining a label_source filter, an insert writer changing its value, a second attach call in the import, the engagement label constant renamed), and 2 checker-side (the absence helper gutted to return False, the string-constant reader gutted to an empty string) -- both of the last two only go red on their positive control, which is exactly why control 7 exists. Every mutant asserts WHICH test must notice and WHICH claim name must appear, so a mutant satisfied by a neighbouring test is rejected as TOO WEAK and the script exits non-zero. The harness takes an exclusive lock because the sandbox executes commands twice, and it restores every touched file from a byte snapshot in a finally block, comparing sha256 afterwards.

P3 PLANNING ROUND (feat/p3-s1-outcome-label-seam, commit a3dbb03c) -- reconnaissance and slice plan, no code yet. The ticket was a blank placeholder (status planning, subtasks [], no prd.md, both jsonl files holding only the example line), so this round produced prd.md with thirty-odd file:line findings, a rewritten framing, four slices, the red lines, the refusals and four open rulings. THE LOAD-BEARING FINDING: the parent ticket lists four things and THREE OF THEM ALREADY EXIST -- offline quality vs online reward is already distinguished in storage (evaluator_samples.label_source is declared as "evaluator" | "engagement" | "human_review", evaluator_config.py:347, with engagement as its own JSONB column), the online reward is already collected for real (creator_note_stats in db/creator_stats.py:70-91 carries views/likes/comments/collects/shares and its own engagement_rate, fed by a 6225-line services/creator_stats/ subsystem with a 1576-line CDP client), LearningSignal -> ModelRevision already has a full lifecycle, and the two personalization stacks ALREADY SHARE A READ SEAM (memory/creator_agent_observations.py:111 implements the CreatorContentObservationSource protocol declared in creator_agent/observations.py:16, consumed by creator_agent/advisor.py:177). Nothing needs to be built. WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING IS TWO CONNECTIONS, and both are proven, not inferred: (1) THE WEAK-LABEL FEED PATH DOES NOT EXIST. The only regular writer of evaluator_samples.engagement is agents/analyst.py:271-280, and its dict comprehension filters five keys (views/likes/collects/comments/shares) that publisher.py NEVER writes -- grep for those literals in publisher.py returns ZERO hits, and all twelve places that assign into publish_result carry error/error_type/recovery/result_known/note/publish_id metadata only. The gate is therefore always false. CORRECTED ON S1 DAY 1 (see prd.md section 9): the auto edge was removed, but analyst is NOT unreachable -- builder.py:187 continues 'It can be reached by resuming the workflow with phase=analyzing', state/modes.py:170/188 both map ANALYZING -> analyst, and api/routes/_wf_application.py:1818 is a complete manual trigger endpoint (assert_thread_owned + a has_analytics idempotence gate + Command(goto=["analyst"])). So the break is NOT 'nobody runs it', it is 'running it still cannot work': publish_result carries none of the five keys, and the manual path reads the same publish-time dict. Corroboration: label_source="engagement" appears ZERO times in backend/. (2) THE REAL METRICS NEVER REACH THE LEARNER. analytics.py contains ZERO references to evaluator_config / backfill_engagement / evaluator_samples / insert_sample, and the linker's product (link_status="linked", written only at analytics.py:894 and :908) is a REQUEST-TIME PROJECTION that is never persisted. evaluator_samples has no platform_post_id column while backfill_engagement(thread_id, ...) keys on thread_id -- so even a willing caller has no key to join on. CONSEQUENCE (assertable): count_labeled_since counts engagement IS NOT NULL, so it is identically 0, which is below MIN_EVOLVE_SAMPLES = 10 (evaluator_config.py:896), so maybe_evolve never leaves the below-threshold branch (evaluator_config.py:976-977) and train_weights / PromptEpoch never advance. THE WHOLE LOOP IS STRUCTURALLY COMPLETE, FULLY TESTED AND GREEN, AND HAS NEVER RUN ONCE -- the purest member of the 'declaration is not execution' family: evaluator_config.py's module docstring promises 'eventually trained from real engagement feedback', analyst.py:263 promises a 'weak label for grader finetuning', publisher.py:351 promises an explicit id match -- three declarations, zero data points. REFRAMING (same shape as P2c's 'not a missing Planner, a missing plan object'): P3 is not missing an Outcome Learning loop, it is missing the two wires that were designed into it. Consequence for slicing: no new module, no new Agent, no cross-module refactor -- each slice only has to make one existing wire actually carry current. SLICES: S1 make the situation visible and stop the bleeding (turn 'the loop never started' into a gate that goes red, and deal with analyst.py's always-empty back-fill, today's biggest source of misinformation). S2 lift the linker out of request-time projection into a reusable form and give evaluator_samples a nullable platform_post_id. S3 close the wire: after creator-stats/sync, back-fill real metrics into evaluator_samples.engagement with label_source="engagement", the first moment maybe_evolve is reachable. S4 the contract and gate condition document (docs/outcome-learning.md). S1's gate must distinguish 'never started' from 'ran and produced zero' -- those two are identical on all real data today (the same family as P2c-S5's 'a claim whose value is zero has no built-in control'), so it has to point at somewhere the thing DOES exist. OPEN RULINGS (all four carry the measured fact that decides them): (1) the parent's 'unify the two personalization stacks into a Memory Fabric' -- the READ side is already unified and no call site today reads both sides, so the write side is NOT consolidated; (2) merging decision-side LearningSignal (feedback-driven, pending_creator_review = human-gated) with engagement weak labels (automatic) would change the human gate's semantics, so NOT merged until a conflicting-conclusion instance exists; (3) whether creator_note_stats should re-drive sample recomputation -- deferred until S3 shows the re-back-fill cost (the table is an upsert and notes keep accruing); (4) MOST IMPORTANT -- what happens to the analyst node now that it is unreachable, since all three of its jobs (content_history metrics, weak-label back-fill, insights) silently stop happening when it does not run, while S1 must answer whether to restore its trigger or hand its duties to capability that already exists elsewhere. ANCHOR DISCIPLINE: every file:line claim in prd.md was programmatically re-checked after writing (51 anchors, each asserting an expected token on the cited line); the first pass caught 10 anchors that had drifted by 1-5 lines, all corrected before commit, and the document's stated counts (6225 / 1576 / 0 / 0 / 0) are re-derived by the same checker rather than copied.
